subject: How to define adjacency matrix when there is an exclave island

messages.author: 79c3b52defbd0096
messages.subject: How to define adjacency matrix when there is an exclave island
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am doing spatiotemporal analysis with Nimble. One of the districts/counties is an exclave island (which lies in the territory of another country), meaning that it has 0 neighbours. 

In my code, I just entered IDs of two districts that seem to be a bit closer to the island, as its neighbours. But when I run the function "buildMCMC( )", I get the error below, which I think is related to the way I defined neighbours of this island (I stand to be corrected).

Here is the error:

Error in CAR_normal_checkNeighborIndWeightLists(neighborIndList, neighborWeightList, :  
neighbor of node u[10] in dcar_normal() distribution are not symmetric with node u[1] 

Thanks in advance!

Regards,

Mwandida.

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: How to define adjacency matrix when there is an exclave island
parts:
Mwandida, the checking of the validity of the neighbourhood structure in the dcar_normal distribution does enforce (and require, for correctness) the the neighbour relationships are symmetric.  That is (lookin at your error message) if u[1] is a neighbour of u[10], then u[10] must also be specified as being a neighbour of u[1].  Take a look at the relationships you specified, and make sure they're symmetric.

If you only added an additional neighbour for the exclave island (0-neighbour) district so that has >0 neighbours, that's not necessary.  You're ok to have districts (regions) with 0 neighbours.

Cheers,
Daniel
